content: As a software developer maintaining the GitHub repository openhwgroup_cvfpu_pr87, you are responsible for analyzing a submitted issue and identifying the exact location in the repository where the issue occurs.

Here is the issue description:
# Bug report: multifmt slice uses wrong FP width for third operand
Hi,
the `fpnew_opgroup_multifmt_slice` uses the wrong FP width for the third operand.
AFAIK the third operand is only used by the `ADDMUL` opgroup, which expects that `operands_i[0]` and `operands_i[1]` have the FP format specified by `src_fmt_i`  and `operands_i[2]` and the result have the FP format `dst_fmt_i`:
https://github.com/openhwgroup/cvfpu/blob/5da3b411f3309d41b39dbc68da7449456f6be444/src/fpnew_fma_multi.sv#L36-L37
Accordingly, the `fpnew_opgroup_multifmt_slice` should use the width of FP format `dst_fmt_i` when assigning the individual elements of `operands_i[2]` to the lane instances. However, the width of `src_fmt_i` is used for all operands:
https://github.com/openhwgroup/cvfpu/blob/5da3b411f3309d41b39dbc68da7449456f6be444/src/fpnew_opgroup_multifmt_slice.sv#L181-L183
As a result, the third operand is incorrect for all lanes (except for the first lane), as shown in the following waveform. The first group of signals shows the `src_fmt_i` (which is `FP16`) and `dst_fmt_i` (which is `FP32`), as well as `operands_i[0]` (for reference) and `operands_i[2]` of the `fpnew_opgroup_multifmt_slice`. The elements of `operands_i[0]` which are 16 bits wide are correctly assigned to the individual `fpnew_fma_multi` instances (as seen in the signal groups below, which show the input operands of the first three instances). However, the elements of `operands_i[2]` which are 32 bits wide are not correctly assigned. The individual elements of these operands are surrounded by rectangles of different colors.
![fpnew_bug_annotated](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9446837/232724219-7daa7d8d-765b-4c12-9f0e-a2083a78c041.png)

Your task is to:
1. Carefully review the issue description and thoroughly analyze the issue to uncover all possible causes.
2. Review the provided code file and identify at least three locations within the file that require inspection or modification to resolve the issue.

Guidelines for Specifying Locations:
1. The locations can be specified as class names, function or method names, or exact line numbers.
2. Line ranges may span across multiple classes or methods if necessary. Ensure all line numbers are accurate and within the valid range of the provided code.

IMPORTANT:
1. Analyze how the provided code file relates to the issue and identify at least three related locations that require modification (e.g., edits, additions) or require inspection (e.g., provide important context).
2. If a new method or class needs to be added to resolve the issue, specify a broader line range that includes surrounding code to provide context and ensure proper placement.
3. Check if any dependencies, helper methods, or global variables should be modified to ensure logical and structural coherence.
4. Check the functionally similar or similarly named methods/classes that might have the same bug or require consistency updates.

Provide the response using the following strict format:

<analysis>
The root cause is in fpnew_opgroup_multifmt_slice.sv: the generate block for the ADDMUL opgroup computes a single “FP_WIDTH” from src_fmt_i and then uses that width for all three operands. However ADDMUL needs operands 0 & 1 packed at src_fmt width and operand 2 (the addend) at dst_fmt width. Consequently:

1. In the ADDMUL slice genblock, the localparam FP_WIDTH must be split into two widths: one for src_fmt_i and one for dst_fmt_i.
2. The bit‐slicing of operands_i[2] in lines ~181–183 must switch from FP_WIDTH (src) to FP_WIDTH_DST (dst).
3. A similar dual‐width change is needed for slicing the is_boxed_i bus for operand 2.
4. The combine counterpart (fpnew_opgroup_multifmt_combine.sv) must also be updated in the result-pack genblock: slicing result_i[2] using dst_fmt width rather than src_fmt.

Each of these areas requires inspection and patching.
</analysis>

<location>
  <class></class>
  <method></method>
  <start_line>160</start_line>
  <end_line>170</end_line>
</location>
<!--
 In fpnew_opgroup_multifmt_slice.sv:  
 The top of the ADDMUL generate block declares:
   localparam int unsigned FP_WIDTH = fpnew_pkg::fp_width(src_fmt_i);
 This must be split into
   localparam int unsigned SRC_FP_WIDTH = fpnew_pkg::fp_width(src_fmt_i);
   localparam int unsigned DST_FP_WIDTH = fpnew_pkg::fp_width(dst_fmt_i);
 so you have two separate widths for slicing operands 0/1 vs. operand 2.
-->

<location>
  <class></class>
  <method></method>
  <start_line>178</start_line>
  <end_line>183</end_line>
</location>
<!--
 In the same ADDMUL genblock of fpnew_opgroup_multifmt_slice.sv:
   assign lane_operands[ lane ][2] =
     operands_i[ lane*FP_WIDTH +: FP_WIDTH ];
 This is exactly lines 181–183. It must change to use DST_FP_WIDTH for the addend:
   assign lane_operands[ lane ][2] =
     operands_i[ lane*DST_FP_WIDTH +: DST_FP_WIDTH ];
-->

<location>
  <class></class>
  <method></method>
  <start_line>184</start_line>
  <end_line>190</end_line>
</location>
<!--
 Also in that ADDMUL genblock, the is_boxed bits for operand 2 use the same FP_WIDTH-derived span:
   assign lane_is_boxed[ lane ][2] =
     is_boxed_i[ fmt ][ 2*FP_WIDTH +: FP_WIDTH ];
 This must also switch to DST_FP_WIDTH:
   assign lane_is_boxed[ lane ][2] =
     is_boxed_i[ fmt ][ 2*DST_FP_WIDTH +: DST_FP_WIDTH ];
-->

<location>

</location>
<!--
 In fpnew_opgroup_multifmt_combine.sv (the mirror image that packs results back out):
 around lines 150–158 there is:
   localparam int unsigned FP_WIDTH = fpnew_pkg::fp_width(src_fmt_o);
 and later
   assign outputs_o[ lane*FP_WIDTH +: FP_WIDTH ] = lane_results[ lane ][2];
 Change it to declare DST_FP_WIDTH = fpnew_pkg::fp_width(dst_fmt_o) and use that width for operand-2/snapping of the ADDMUL result.
-->
